name.en: Alaska Route 1 — Sterling, Seward, Glenn and Tok Cut-Off
name.zh: 阿拉斯加 1 号公路（斯特灵、苏华德、格伦公路与托克支线）

tagline.en: Homer to Tok by way of Anchorage, under four different names
tagline.zh: 从霍默经安克雷奇到托克，沿途换过四个路名

start.en: Homer Ferry Terminal, at the tip of the Homer Spit
start.zh: 霍默沙嘴尽头的霍默渡轮码头

end.zh: 托克，与阿拉斯加公路（AK 2）相接

en: AK 1 is a route number laid over a chain of separately built and separately named roads. From the Homer Spit it follows the Sterling Highway up the Kenai Peninsula, turns north onto the Seward Highway at Tern Lake, runs through Anchorage on a pair of one-way city streets, becomes the Glenn Highway out of town, touches the Richardson Highway near Glennallen, and finishes along the Tok Cut-Off. Almost nobody in Alaska calls any of it "Route 1".

The best-known stretch is the Seward Highway between Anchorage and Girdwood, pinched between the cliffs of Chugach State Park, the Alaska Railroad and the tidal water of Turnagain Arm. It is the only road connection from Anchorage to the Kenai Peninsula, which means commuter traffic, freight, tour buses and people stopping abruptly to look at Dall sheep all share the same two lanes.

East of Anchorage the character changes completely. The Glenn Highway follows the braided Matanuska River past hanging glaciers and roadhouses, climbs to Eureka Summit, and then crosses into the wide, thinly populated Copper River country on its way to the Alaska Highway.
zh: AK 1 只是一个编号，铺在一串各自修建、各自命名的道路之上。它从霍默沙嘴出发，沿斯特灵公路北上基奈半岛，在特恩湖转上苏华德公路向北，在安克雷奇借一对单行市街穿城而过，出城后变成格伦公路，在格伦纳伦附近与理查森公路交汇，最后沿托克支线收尾。在阿拉斯加，几乎没人把其中任何一段叫作「1 号公路」。
最出名的是安克雷奇到吉德伍德之间的苏华德公路段，夹在丘加奇州立公园的峭壁、阿拉斯加铁路与特纳甘湾的潮水之间。它是安克雷奇通往基奈半岛的唯一陆路联系，也就是说通勤车流、货运、旅游大巴，以及为看白大角羊而突然停车的人，全都挤在同样的两条车道上。
安克雷奇以东，性格完全变了。格伦公路沿辫状的马塔努斯卡河而行，经过悬冰川与路边旅舍，爬上尤里卡岭，随后进入辽阔而人口稀疏的铜河地区，一路通往阿拉斯加公路。

en: The Turnagain Arm section is being rebuilt, and the documentation explains why better than any description could. Alaska DOT&PF's Safer Seward Highway proposal would reconstruct mileposts 98.5 to 118 as a four-lane divided highway to a 55 mph design speed, straightening six curves between mileposts 105 and 110 and adding a separated multi-use path. The stated objective is to remove the Safety Corridor designation that has applied between Anchorage and Girdwood.

Getting there means cutting into rock. About 40 percent of the twenty-mile stretch would require rock cuts on the cliff side, and the draft assessment identifies roughly 120 acres of fill in Turnagain Arm, about half of it designated critical habitat for the endangered Cook Inlet beluga whale. Climbers objected at public hearings that the blasting would remove much of the rock and ice climbing accessible from the road.

Rockfall has been a problem here since the highway was built. Mitigation installed in 1992 between mileposts 104 and 114 was damaged or destroyed by later rockfall, notably after the 2018 Anchorage earthquake; nine slopes were identified as safety concerns and most were treated again with bolts, dowels, attenuators and draped mesh in 2023.
zh: 特纳甘湾路段正在重建，而相关文件比任何描述都更能说明原因。阿拉斯加州交通与公共设施部的「更安全的苏华德公路」方案拟将 98.5 至 118 英里路段重建为设计车速 55 英里／小时的四车道分隔公路，把 105 至 110 英里之间的六处弯道拉直，并增设一条分离式多用途步道。明确目标是取消安克雷奇至吉德伍德之间一直沿用的「安全走廊」标识。
要做到这一点就得开山。这二十英里路段中约四成需要在崖侧进行岩石开挖，环评草案还认定将在特纳甘湾内填方约 120 英亩，其中约一半属于濒危的库克湾白鲸的关键栖息地。攀登者在公开听证会上提出反对，认为爆破会毁掉大部分从公路即可抵达的岩壁与冰壁线路。
自公路建成以来，落石一直是难题。1992 年在 104 至 114 英里之间设置的防护措施，后来被落石损坏或摧毁，2018 年安克雷奇地震之后尤为严重；共有九处坡面被列为安全隐患，2023 年多数又以锚杆、锚钉、消能装置和悬挂钢丝网重新处理了一遍。

en: Two segments of AK 1 carry scenic designations and they are the ones worth planning a day around. The Seward Highway holds a triple designation — USDA Forest Service Scenic Byway, Alaska Scenic Byway and All-American Road — and the Glenn Highway National Scenic Byway follows the Matanuska River for over half its length, ending at Eureka Summit where four mountain ranges are visible at once.

All of it is paved and open all year, but the Anchorage–Girdwood stretch is where attention matters most: few passing opportunities, tidal mudflats on one side, and an avalanche zone at Windy Corner between mileposts 105 and 107. Winter brings icefall as well as rockfall, and the road has been closed by both.

The pull-offs are the point. Potter Marsh, Beluga Point and Bird Point all sit within the reconstruction area, and the design keeps them; the alternative to using them is stopping on a shoulder in traffic that does not expect it.
zh: AK 1 有两段获得了景观道路认定，值得专门安排一天。苏华德公路拥有三重身份——美国农业部林务局景观道路、阿拉斯加州景观道路，以及「全美道路」；格伦公路国家景观道路则有一半以上路程沿马塔努斯卡河而行，终点尤里卡岭可同时望见四条山脉。
全线铺装、全年通行，但安克雷奇至吉德伍德一段最需要专注：超车机会很少，一侧是潮汐泥滩，105 至 107 英里的风角还有一处雪崩区。冬季除落石之外还有落冰，两者都曾造成封路。
路边观景点才是重点。波特沼泽、白鲸角和鸟角都在重建范围之内，方案保留了它们；不用它们的替代做法，就是在毫无预期的车流中停在路肩上。

label.zh: 苏华德公路的景观认定

value.en: 127 miles, holding three designations: USDA Forest Service Scenic Byway, Alaska Scenic Byway and All-American Road
value.zh: 127 英里，同时拥有三项认定：美国农业部林务局景观道路、阿拉斯加州景观道路、全美道路

value.en: 135 miles, following the Matanuska River for over half its length
value.zh: 135 英里，其中一半以上路程沿马塔努斯卡河而行

label.en: Cost of the Safer Seward Highway reconstruction
label.zh: 「更安全的苏华德公路」重建工程造价

why.en: The project was still at draft environmental assessment stage when this was written and no construction cost estimate could be verified from DOT&PF. Publishing a number before the agency does would be a guess.
why.zh: 本条目撰写时，该项目仍处于环境评估草案阶段，未能从州交通与公共设施部查证到施工造价估算。在主管机构公布之前给出数字只能是猜测。

why.en: AK 1 spans an urban freeway in Anchorage and single-lane rural road in the Copper River basin. Alaska DOT&PF publishes counts per station rather than per route, and no route-level figure could be verified this session.
why.zh: AK 1 既包含安克雷奇的城市高速路段，也包含铜河流域的乡村单车道路段。阿拉斯加州交通与公共设施部按观测站而非按路线发布交通量，本次查证未能取得全线数据。

value.en: The Anchorage–Girdwood segment carries a state Safety Corridor designation after a high rate of serious-injury and fatal crashes; removing it is the reconstruction project's stated objective
value.zh: 因重伤与致死事故率偏高，安克雷奇至吉德伍德路段被列为州级「安全走廊」；取消该标识是重建项目的明确目标

conditionFigures.source: Alaska DOT&PF, Safer Seward Highway project fact sheet, January 2026

value.en: Windy Corner Avalanche Zone at mileposts 105–107; nine rock slopes between mileposts 104 and 114 identified as safety concerns and retreated in 2023
value.zh: 105 至 107 英里为风角雪崩区；104 至 114 英里之间有九处坡面被列为安全隐患，并于 2023 年重新处理

conditionFigures.source: Alaska DOT&PF, Safer Seward Highway Draft Environmental Assessment, December 2025

timeline.en: DOT&PF installs rockfall mitigation on slopes between mileposts 104 and 114 of the Seward Highway.
timeline.zh: 州交通与公共设施部在苏华德公路 104 至 114 英里的坡面设置落石防护设施。

timeline.en: The Anchorage earthquake damages or destroys much of the existing rockfall protection along Turnagain Arm.
timeline.zh: 安克雷奇地震损坏或摧毁了特纳甘湾沿线大部分既有落石防护设施。

timeline.en: Rockfall mitigation is rebuilt at most of the nine identified slopes.
timeline.zh: 九处认定坡面中的多数完成落石防护重建。

timeline.en: DOT&PF publishes the draft environmental assessment for a four-lane divided rebuild between mileposts 98.5 and 118.
timeline.zh: 州交通与公共设施部公布 98.5 至 118 英里改建为四车道分隔公路的环境评估草案。
